title: Partner origins & contract clause extract request
text:
Partner origins & contract clause extract request

['From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ava Solutions Legal <legal@avasolutions.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Partner origins & contract clause extract request

Hi Ava / legal team,

Thanks for continuing to work with us on the Novamed compliance sweep. We have a quick, scoped ask to close out the CAIQ/SIG row coverage for third-party origins and contractual controls. Can you send a concise CSV and a PDF excerpt that covers the following for all hosted/inference partners you depend on (direct and transit):

- Partner name and primary point of contact
- Hosting region(s) (cloud region and country of data residency)
- Whether they are a subprocessor under your contract (yes/no)
- Short excerpt (1–3 sentences) of the contractual clause that allows/subcontracts that processor (redact commercial rates if needed)
- Note if any partner uses a downstream key management provider (KMS) or ephemeral key service and where the keys are resident

Ideally: partner-origins.csv (columns: partner, contact, region, subproc, clause_ref, kms_residency) and clause-extract.pdf with the exact clause language (redactions allowed).

Target turnaround: EOD Tue (2026-09-15) so we can ingest into the SIG matrix and produce a one-page summary for Novamed procurement. If you foresee any pushback on sharing clause language, flag which clauses are NDAs and we can propose a handling approach (sealed review / redline sight-only).

Thanks — we appreciate the quick help on this.

Marcus Lin
Senior Manager, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
', "From: Ava Solutions Legal <legal@avasolutions.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Partner origins & contract clause extract request

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear template. We attached a CSV and a PDF with clause excerpts; see attached:
- partner-origins.csv (partner list + regions + subproc flag + KMS residency column)
- clause-extract.pdf (selected contract passages, redacted for commercial rates)

Quick notes / caveats:
- A few transit partners (listed in the CSV) are engaged via our integrator contract and are treated as permitted subprocessors under clause 6.3. We included the clause reference but redacted party-specific pricing lines.
- For two partners (EdgeCloud Platform and LumenKey), we can confirm KMS is provided by a downstream provider; LumenKey keys are resident in EU (Ireland) per their info sheet. EdgeCloud has a multi-region model — we marked regions where Novamed data would be stored if requested.
- We flagged three partners where the contract prevents clause-level redaction removal without a mutual NDA; we included a short justification in the PDF and a proposed sealed-review workflow if Novamed needs to see the full language.

If you'd like, we can also provide the canonical contract IDs and dates (they're in our procurement system) so you can map them to the SIG rows.

Best,
Ava Patel
Legal Operations Manager
Ava Solutions
legal@avasolutions.com

", 'From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Solutions Legal <legal@avasolutions.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T11:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Partner origins & contract clause extract request

Thanks Ava — CSV looks good at a glance. Couple of follow-ups before we mark SIG rows as complete: 

1) For any partner marked as "subproc = yes", can you include the contract execution date and whether the subproc right is delegated (i.e., does their contract allow them to appoint downstream subprocessors without our prior written consent)? A short flag (delegated_yes/delegated_no) will do.

2) For partners that use downstream KMS/ephemeral key providers, can you confirm whether Greenwood (a vendor we commonly see) is in the chain? If so, we need key residency and whether the upstream contract requires HSM-backed keys.

3) If there are any hosting regions that would require EU data residency for Novamed (they stipulate EU-only for certain records), please mark those rows as "EU_only = true" so the compliance summary can auto-filter.

If it's easier, we can accept a short supplemental CSV with these three columns; otherwise we can annotate the original.

Karthik
Principal, Security & Risk
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
', "From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Partner origins & contract clause extract request

Ava — thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachments.

Sooj and Karthik — Karthik's follow-ups are spot on. Ava, if you can add the three columns (contract_date, delegated_yes/no, EU_only flag) either inline or as a supplemental CSV that would let us finish the SIG mapping today. Once we have that I'll upload the summary to the shared Drive link and create the HubSpot artifact for Novamed (link below).

Action items:
- Ava: supplemental CSV with contract_date / delegated flag / EU_only by EOD (2026-09-15)
- Soojin: I'll assign you the SIG row review once the supplemental CSV is in — can you spot-check clause excerpts for scope?
- Karthik: please prepare an excerpt note for any partners that show delegated subproc rights; we'll propose a follow-up question template for procurement.

Drive upload link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cPartnerOrigins
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HD-1192

Thanks all — we'll close this loop today.

Marcus Lin
Senior Manager, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
